Hi Kimberly,

I hope you had a good week. I'm planning my return from medical leave and wanted to start the discussion about a phased schedule and a few workplace accommodations recommended by my doctor. My proposed plan is: 

- Start part-time (20 hours/week) for the first 4 weeks, then 30 hours/week for 2 weeks, then return to full time the week after (if cleared).
- Work-from-home first two weeks to avoid the commute while I rebuild stamina.
- Ergonomic assessment + temporary back support chair for my desk.
- Flexibility to shift core hours by one hour on heavy symptom days.

I have a doctor's note that outlines restrictions (light lifting, max 4 hours of on-site consecutive desk time at first). I can attach that to HR — I included it as an attachment on this thread.

Target return date: Monday, April 12 (if that still works for staffing). Please let me know what information HR needs and whether an occupational health consult is preferred.

Thanks,
Evelyn

From: Dr. Priya Shah <priya.shah@occupationalhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Occupational health assessment — Evelyn Hart (summary)

Hi Kimberly and Evelyn,

Thanks for the referral. I conducted a brief tele-assessment with Evelyn and reviewed the clinical note you provided. Summary and recommended accommodations: 

- Recommend a graduated return-to-work over 6 weeks: Weeks 1–2: 3 days remote + 2 short (4-hour) on-site days; Weeks 3–4: 4 days remote + 1 full on-site day (6 hours); Weeks 5–6: 30 hours/week with increasing on-site time; full-time thereafter if tolerated.
- Provide an ergonomic chair with lumbar support and a monitor arm (to reduce neck flexion).
- Limit heavy lifting and onsite manual handling for 8 weeks.
- Allow one 15–30 minute break mid-afternoon for prescribed exercises.

I've attached a one-page report (OH_report_EHart.pdf) with the clinical rationale and suggested accommodations for HR and the engineering team to review. If the team needs an on-site assessment, we can schedule one the week of April 5.

Best regards,
Dr. Priya Shah
Occupational Health Services
Attachment: OH_report_EHart.pdf

- Equipment: ergonomic chair (temporary for 8 weeks), monitor arm, laptop docking station, and a sit-stand cushion.

Dev — please confirm coverage plan for the two-week 20-hour period; if we need to shift timelines by a week to avoid blocking a critical launch, say so by Monday, 2026-04-05. Attached: phased_return_schedule_2026-04-12.pdf and HR_return_form.pdf (completed).

Kimberly
